title: Garlic Naan Tandoor Bread

seo.title: Garlic Naan Recipe: Authentic Tandoor Bread at Home
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of homemade Garlic Naan with our authentic recipe! Learn to make soft, flavorful tandoor bread at home, perfect for Indian meals.
seo.h1: Authentic Garlic Naan Tandoor Bread Recipe
seo.imageAlt: Freshly baked garlic naan bread, golden brown with chopped garlic and cilantro, ready to serve with Indian food.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy warm, fluffy Garlic Naan, brushed with butter and garlic, fresh from your kitchen!

description: Garlic Naan is a beloved Indian leavened flatbread, traditionally baked in a tandoor oven, known for its soft, chewy texture and irresistible garlic flavor. This recipe brings the authentic taste of restaurant-style naan to your home kitchen, perfect for scooping up curries or enjoying on its own. With aromatic garlic and fresh cilantro, each bite is a delightful burst of classic Indian flavors.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the warm water, granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until a frothy layer forms on top, indicating the yeast is active. This is crucial for a fluffy naan.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough Mixture
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour and salt. Create a well in the center of the dry ingredients. Pour in the activated yeast mixture, warm milk, plain yogurt, and 1 tablespoon of the melted ghee or butter into the well.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Mix the ingredients with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes. Continue kneading until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. Form it into a ball.

instructions.title: First Rise of the Dough
instructions.text: Lightly grease a clean bowl with a little oil. Place the dough ball in the bowl, turning it once to coat all sides. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel. Let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare Garlic Butter and Portion Dough
instructions.text: While the dough is rising, prepare the garlic butter by combining the remaining 2 tablespoons of melted ghee or butter with the minced garlic and chopped fresh cilantro in a small bowl. Once the dough has risen, gently punch it down to release the air. Divide the dough into 8 equal portions.

instructions.title: Shape and Cook the Naan
instructions.text: Preheat a cast-iron skillet or tawa over high heat until smoking hot, or preheat your oven to its highest setting with a pizza stone inside. Take one dough portion and roll it out on a lightly floured surface into an oval or teardrop shape, about 6-8 inches long and 1/4 inch thick. Brush one side of the rolled naan generously with the prepared garlic butter mixture. Place the naan, garlic-side down, onto the hot skillet or pizza stone. Cook for 1-2 minutes until large bubbles form on the surface and the bottom is golden brown with charred spots. Flip the naan and cook the other side for another 1-2 minutes until it puffs up and is lightly browned.

instructions.title: Serve Fresh
instructions.text: Remove the cooked naan from the skillet or oven. Brush immediately with a little extra garlic butter for added flavor and shine. Repeat the shaping and cooking process with the remaining dough portions. Serve the garlic naan hot and fresh alongside your favorite Indian curries or dishes.

tips: For an authentic tandoor-like experience, ensure your cast iron skillet or tawa is smoking hot before placing the naan. This high heat is crucial for achieving the characteristic puff and slightly charred spots.
Using plain whole milk yogurt and warm milk helps create a soft and pliable dough. If you don't have ghee, unsalted butter can be used, but ghee adds a richer, nutty flavor.
Naan is best served immediately when hot and fresh. If you have leftovers, lightly sprinkle with water, wrap in foil, and reheat in a warm oven or microwave for a few seconds to regain softness.
